subject.title: Bug: Poe image/video-output models are accepted in config but fail at runtime (Nano Banana 400, Veo/Sora fallback)

question: Should OpenClaw reject non-text-output models when configured as chat/session models, or add first-class output-modality metadata and runtime support for image/video chat outputs?
rationale: Both paths are plausible, but the choice changes public config semantics, provider ownership, and media-generation routing, so automation should not choose it from source inspection alone.

options.title: Reject unsupported chat output now
options.body: Add a clear unsupported-output diagnostic for image/video-output models selected as chat/session models and direct users to image_generate or video_generate until first-class support exists.

options.title: Add output-modality support
options.body: Extend config/catalog metadata plus runtime and channel rendering so selected models can intentionally produce image/video outputs in session flow.

options.title: Docs-only clarification
options.body: Document that media generation must use generation tools while accepting the current custom-provider runtime behavior and its support burden.

recommendation.title: Reject unsupported chat output now
recommendation.body: Add a clear unsupported-output diagnostic for image/video-output models selected as chat/session models and direct users to image_generate or video_generate until first-class support exists.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans provider/model config, fallback policy, and media-generation direction where recent history shows relevant ownership.
